blocks.content: # COMPASS: Continuous Monitoring of Postpartum Blood Pressure

blocks.title: About the Study
blocks.content:
The **COMPASS** study (Continuous Monitoring of Postpartum Blood Pressure for Assessment and Shifting of Cardiovascular Risk) is a prospective, multicenter, randomised controlled trial within the **EXIT-CVD** research consortium, co-funded by the **European Union Innovative Health Initiative (IHI)**.
Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) affect approximately 10% of pregnancies, carrying significant risks for maternal and neonatal health, including stroke and pre-eclampsia. Postpartum hypertension remains inadequately monitored despite contributing substantially to maternal morbidity and mortality. Emerging evidence indicates that postpartum BP control critically influences long-term cardiovascular health, with interventions potentially providing durable risk reductions.
COMPASS evaluates the feasibility, clinical effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness of continuous BP monitoring via validated wearable technology (Huawei D2 Watch) to improve postpartum blood pressure control.

blocks.title: Study Design
blocks.content:
COMPASS is a prospective, multicenter, randomised controlled trial comparing:

- **Control group:** Standard postpartum care
- **Intervention group:** Continuous wearable BP monitoring (Huawei D2 Watch) plus digital assistant-supported clinician titration via Megi-Mum and the RADAR platform

The study recruits 100 postpartum women across three clinical sites: **King's College Hospital**, **St Thomas' Hospital**, and **UMC Utrecht**. Participation lasts approximately 6 months.

blocks.title: The Role of Onsentia & RADAR-base
blocks.content:
Onsentia powers the digital data collection and remote monitoring infrastructure for the COMPASS study using the open-source RADAR-base platform.
By combining active patient-reported outcome measurements (aRMT) with passive sensor and wearable data collection (pRMT), Onsentia and RADAR-base enable multi-source, scalable, real-time remote monitoring and data integration.
**Huawei Health** provides continuous blood pressure monitoring via the D2 Watch. **Megi-Mum** delivers AI-powered personalised cardiovascular and maternal heart care assessments, and **CogStack** assists in identifying eligible participants from medical records.

blocks.title: Part of EXIT-CVD
blocks.content:
COMPASS is one of the "early exit" studies within the EXIT-CVD consortium. EXIT-CVD is a five-year research project that brings together 42 partners across 17 countries to transform how cardiovascular disease is detected, monitored and treated. It is led by **UMCG** and **Philips**, with a total budget of EUR 27.6 million.
The study sponsor is **King's College London**, a public research university based in London, United Kingdom.

blocks.title: More Information
blocks.content:
For more details about the EXIT-CVD project, visit [exitcvd.eu](https://exitcvd.eu/).
This website is hosted by King's College London on its secure health research platform called RADAR-base.
